# E044 -- Twitch Brand Guidelines (Speedrun)

## Metadata
- **Company:** Twitch (Amazon)
- **Industry:** Streaming / Gaming
- **Year:** 2019
- **Source file:** twitch_guidelines_speedrun_v1-0-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 19
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-13

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "Identity Guidelines (Speedrun Edition)" V1.0, dated 10.31.19
- Brand manifesto: "Not everyone's going to get it" -- anti-mainstream positioning
- Core philosophy: "multiplayer is everything -- our how and our why"
- Community-first: "collective cast of millions going all-in to make moments together"
- Embraces unpredictability: "We don't always know what's next, and we like it that way"
- "This started as a place to stream. Together, we're making it Twitch."

## Logo
- Wordmark and Glitch (icon) are the two primary marks
- **Internal lockup:** logo with internal Twitch sub-brands, spaced by cap height / X-height
- **Partnership lockup:** logo with external partner logos, center-aligned
- Extruded Wordmark variant exists
- **Logo color pairings** (only four allowed for core communications):
  1. Twitch Purple on Ice
  2. Black Ops on Twitch Purple
  3. Twitch Purple on Black
  - Solid backgrounds only for core communications

## Typography
- **Roobert** -- brand typeface, six weights: Light, Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold, Heavy
- 12 styles total including full italic set
- Primary weights: Regular, Medium, Bold, Semibold; Light and Heavy for special instances
- Type scale examples:
  - Headline: Roobert SemiBold 80/80/-20
  - Highlight/Call Out: Roobert Large 30/33/-15
  - Body: Roobert Medium 16/20/-10
  - Body Small: Roobert Medium 11/14/0

## Color
- **Core Palette** (3 swatches):
  - **Twitch Purple:** #9146FF / RGB 145, 70, 255 / PMS 814C / CMYK 57, 60, 0, 0
  - **Black Ops:** #000000 / PMS Black 6C / CMYK 100, 80, 40, 90
  - **Ice:** #F0F0FF / PMS 656C / CMYK 10, 4, 2, 1
- **Secondary Palette** -- massive 30-color system with gaming-themed names:
  - Muted tones: Ice, Jiggle (#FAB4FF), Worm (#FACDCD), Isabelle (#FEEE85), Droid (#BEFAE1), Wipe Out (#00C8AF)
  - Mid tones: Smoke (#BFABFF), Widow (#FC6675), Peach (#FFCA5F), Pac-Man (#57BEE6), Felicia (#0014A5)
  - Vivid tones: Dragon (#8205B4), Cuddle (#FA1ED2), Bandit (#FF6905), Lightning (#FAFA19), K.O. (#BEFF00), Mega (#00FAFA)
  - Dark tones: Nights (#41145F), Osu (#BE0078), Sniper (#FA2828), Egg (#00FA05), Legend (#69FFC3), Zero (#1E69FF)
  - Accent: Smoke (#D2D2E6)
- "When designing for digital, use RGB. When designing for IRL, PMS is preferred. CMYK is the acronym of last resort."

- Color pairings create a distinctive visual language

## Tone of Voice
- Irreverent, community-driven, gaming-native
- Self-referential humor: "And for some reason, by Bob Ross too"
- Gaming vocabulary woven into guidelines: "speedrun", "turbo mode", "ultimate move"
- Color names reference gaming culture: Pac-Man, K.O., Mega, Sniper, Dragon, Zero
- Direct address to reader in casual voice

## Outliers
- **"Speedrun Edition"** framing -- the guidelines themselves are branded with gaming vocabulary
- 30-color secondary palette is one of the largest encountered, all with gaming/pop culture names
- Rich black specification (100, 80, 40, 90) is extremely dense
- Only 19 pages but packs enormous color system density
- Brand manifesto is unusually philosophical and counter-cultural for a tech platform
- PMS colors include fluorescent/neon inks (PMS 814C, 806C, 802C, 803C) -- indicates willingness to use specialty printing
- Ice (#F0F0FF) as a near-white with blue tint rather than pure white is distinctive

## Quality Score
- **4/5** -- Punchy, personality-rich guidelines with an exceptionally detailed color system and clear typography rules; the "Speedrun" format is efficient and on-brand; loses a point for minimal application examples and no photography/graphics guidance, but the personality and color depth are outstanding
